messages:
Diego: Hi all  I'm about to open my first PR to tweak a small log line in the runtime. Quick questions: do we need a changelog entry for tiny infra-only stuff? Also who normally merges low-risk PRs?

Hannah: If it's infra-only and doesn't change behavior, we usually skip the user-facing changelog but add a short note in the PR description under 'Internal notes'. For merges: any approver listed in CODEOWNERS can merge, otherwise ping a core infra reviewer (I can if nobody else is free). :wave:

Ethan: Add a single unit test if it affects observable behaviour. If it's purely cosmetic in logs, add a comment in the code explaining why. CI will still run lint + unit matrix, so run `make lint && ./scripts/test.sh unit` locally to avoid obvious failures.

Diego: Good call. What about backporting tiny fixes to the stable branch?

Mira: Backport only if the bug impacts production customers or released images. For logs/telemetry tweaks we usually land on main and schedule a backport only when a release manager asks. Add a `needs-backport` label if you think it might be needed.

Hannah: Also, small PR etiquette: 1) one concern per PR, 2) keep diffs <200 lines if possible, 3) put a short repro or example in the description. Makes reviews faster.

Diego: Who's a good reviewer for runtime logging? I don't want to ping too many people.

Ethan: Try @Mira first (runtime infra), then @Hannah if it touches pipelines. If your CODEOWNERS auto-suggests someone else, include them.

Mira: On turnaround: aim for 48 hours for non-urgent reviews. If it's urgent, add `priority/urgent` in the PR and mention a reviewer in the thread. For anything that could impact latency or memory, label `runtime-impact` so QA can run the staging checks.

release-bot: FYI: when the PR merges, ensure you format the merge commit message as `fix(runtime): short desc` (or `chore(runtime):` for non-functional changes). That helps release notes automation.

Diego: Perfect. I'll run lint+unit, include an "Internal notes" section instead of changelog, label `runtime-impact` only if I touch performance code, and ping @Mira. Thanks! :thumbsup:
